claudeTmux.refreshMs.description: How often (ms) the side-bar mirror refreshes the tmux pane.

claudeTmux.claudeArgs.description: Arguments passed to `claude` when starting or resuming a session.

claudeTmux.codexArgs.description: Arguments passed to `codex` when starting or resuming a session. `--no-alt-screen` preserves terminal scrollback.

claudeTmux.codexFullAccess.description: Start and resume Codex with Full Access (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`). This disables approval prompts and sandbox protection; turn it off when working in an untrusted repository.

claudeTmux.codexHooks.description: Pass Codex's native lifecycle hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, Stop) at launch, so Codex reports working / needs input / done as ground truth instead of leaving them to screen heuristics. The hooks are passed per launch with -c and never written into your config.toml. Codex asks once to trust the hook commands ("N hooks need review" — press t); until you do, they stay inactive and the notify program still reports done. Requires claudeTmux.stateHooks. Needs Codex 0.147 or newer.

claudeTmux.codexReadClaudeRules.description: Use per-launch developer instructions to make Codex recursively read every Markdown file under workspace `.claude`. The files are not modified. An explicit developer_instructions value in codexArgs takes precedence.

claudeTmux.opencodeArgs.description: Arguments passed to `opencode` when starting or resuming a session. `--auto` auto-approves permissions that are not explicitly denied; remove it to be prompted instead.

claudeTmux.opencodeSessionPrefix.description: OpenCode tmux session prefix. Session = <prefix><folder name> (e.g. tmux_opencode_my-project).

claudeTmux.hermesArgs.description: Arguments passed to `hermes` (Nous Research) when starting or resuming a session. `--cli` runs the classic REPL, which keeps real tmux scrollback in the mirror; use `--tui` for the Ink terminal UI instead (an alternate-screen app, so tmux keeps no scrollback for it). `--yolo` bypasses dangerous-command approval prompts — remove it to be asked. The persistent approval policy is `approvals.mode` in ~/.hermes/config.yaml.

claudeTmux.hermesSessionPrefix.description: Hermes tmux session prefix. Session = <prefix><folder name> (e.g. tmux_hermes_my-project).

claudeTmux.piArgs.description: Arguments passed to `pi` (Earendil) when starting or resuming a session. Empty by default, and deliberately so: pi ships no sandbox and no per-tool approval prompts, so there is no permission flag to bypass — the agent already acts freely. The one prompt pi does show is a first-run project-trust question, which decides whether to load the REPOSITORY's own .pi settings, extensions and skills; add `-a` to answer it automatically for every run, or answer it once in the pane and pi remembers the folder.

claudeTmux.piSessionPrefix.description: Pi tmux session prefix. Session = <prefix><folder name> (e.g. tmux_pi_my-project).

claudeTmux.antigravityArgs.description: Arguments passed to `agy` (Google Antigravity) when starting or resuming a session. Antigravity exposes no state-hook mechanism, so its live state is inferred from the pane.

claudeTmux.antigravitySessionPrefix.description: Antigravity tmux session prefix. Session = <prefix><folder name> (e.g. tmux_agy_my-project).

claudeTmux.devinArgs.description: Arguments passed to `devin` (Cognition Devin CLI) when starting or resuming a session.

claudeTmux.devinSessionPrefix.description: Devin tmux session prefix. Session = <prefix><folder name> (e.g. tmux_devin_my-project).

claudeTmux.sessionPrefix.description: tmux session name prefix. Session = <prefix><folder name> (e.g. tmux_claude_my-project).

claudeTmux.codexSessionPrefix.description: Codex tmux session prefix. Session = <prefix><folder name> (e.g. tmux_codex_my-project).

claudeTmux.scrollbackLines.description: Maximum tmux history lines captured for scrolling in the side-bar mirror.

claudeTmux.fontFamily.description: Font for the mirror. Empty = inherit terminal.integrated.fontFamily (so Nerd Font / Powerline glyphs match your real terminal).

claudeTmux.fontSize.description: Font size for the mirror in px. 0 = inherit terminal.integrated.fontSize (fallback 12).

claudeTmux.autoResume.description: When the side bar opens and no Claude session is running, automatically resume the folder's most recent Claude conversation. Disabled by default so tabs only appear after an explicit start or an existing tmux session is detected.

claudeTmux.transport.description: How tmux is driven. auto: persistent control-mode client with push notifications, falling back to a pipe-pane tap, then polling. control: control mode only. pipe: pipe-pane output tap. poll: classic polling only.

claudeTmux.fileLinks.description: Detect file paths like src/foo.js:42 in the mirror and open them in the editor with Cmd/Ctrl+click.

claudeTmux.promptHistory.description: Record submitted prompt lines (reconstructed from keystrokes, never from agent output) for Alt+Up recall. Stored in workspace state; clear with the 'Clear prompt history' command.

claudeTmux.statusBarItems.description: Show a single status bar item for the active agent (all present agents listed in its tooltip; click to cycle focus). Off hides it entirely.

claudeTmux.notifyPrompts.description: When a hidden or background agent asks a question, raise a notification; numbered menu options become answer buttons (always explicit, never automatic).

claudeTmux.stateHooks.description: Launch Claude with generated lifecycle hooks and Codex with a notify program that stamp ground-truth state (working / needs-input / done, current tool) into tmux pane options. Skipped when your own --settings or notify configuration is present.

claudeTmux.telemetry.description: Tail the CLIs' local JSONL transcripts for tokens, model, turn count and current tool (footer chips and status bar tooltips). Local file reads only; nothing leaves your machine.

claudeTmux.eventLog.description: Record session, turn and handoff events to .claude/agentmux/ledger.jsonl (powers the Timeline and crash-safe handoff recovery).

claudeTmux.tmuxStatusBar.description: Set the agent session's tmux status-right to show AgentMux facts (agent, live state, current tool) for anyone attached in a real terminal.

claudeTmux.fileChannel.description: Exchange handoff briefings, acknowledgements and arbiter answers through .claude/agentmux/ files instead of pasting/scraping the terminal (pane markers remain the automatic fallback). .claude stays the only coordination medium between the agents.

claudeTmux.handoffDiffChars.description: Include up to this many characters of real diff hunks (git diff --unified=1) in the handoff briefing. 0 disables the hunks section.

claudeTmux.handoffTodoFile.description: Workspace-relative task file whose content (capped) is included in handoff briefings. Empty disables.

claudeTmux.handoffVerifyCommand.description: Optional command (e.g. 'npm run check') executed once at handoff-draft time, in the workspace, with a 60s timeout; its output tail is included in the briefing. Requires a trusted workspace. Empty disables.

enumDescriptions: Map ANSI colours onto the VS Code terminal theme, so the mirror matches the rest of the editor.
Use the classic xterm palette, so the mirror shows the colours the program actually asked for — what you would see in a real terminal.
claudeTmux.ansiPalette.description: Which palette the mirror uses for ANSI colours.

claudeTmux.detectionRules.markdownDescription:
Per-agent detection rules used when an agent reports no lifecycle state. Keys are agent ids (claude, codex, opencode, hermes, pi, antigravity, devin, or the id of any `claudeTmux.customAgents` entry). Each agent may set `needsInput`, `working` and `hold`; the same keys nested under `title` are matched against the pane title instead and are evaluated first.

An entry is a case-insensitive regular expression, an array of expressions that must **all** match, or `{ "region": "foot", "match": "..." }` to match somewhere other than the list default. Regions: `body` (the last 12 lines minus the prompt box — the default for needsInput, and what stops your own typing from reading as the agent asking), `tail` (the last 12 lines, default for working and hold), `foot` (the last 5 lines, i.e. the mode/status line), `head` (the first 20 lines), `prompt` (the prompt box), `dialog` (below the last rule the TUI drew), `screen`, `title`.

A `hold` rule freezes the status instead of setting one — that is how a transcript viewer or a settings picker stops the decay timer from walking a working agent down to idle. A provided array REPLACES the built-in list, so `[]` disables a noisy rule. Run **AgentMux: Explain the active agent's state** to see every loaded rule and which one matched.

hold.description: Rules that freeze the status instead of setting one: a transcript viewer, a settings picker, anything covering the pane with chrome that describes itself rather than the agent.

title.description: Rules matched against the pane title (what the TUI wrote with OSC 0/2) instead of the screen.

claudeTmux.customAgents.markdownDescription:
Free mode — extra agent tabs declared here instead of shipped in a release. Two shapes:

- **Launch** `{ "id": "aider", "label": "Aider", "command": "aider", "args": "--yes" }` — AgentMux manages it exactly like a built-in agent: its own tmux session, presence, status, input, handoffs, arbiter and cleanup.
- **Mirror** `{ "id": "build", "label": "Build", "session": "my-build-loop" }` — the tab mirrors a tmux session **you** started. AgentMux never creates, restarts or cleans up such a session; it only shows it and types into it, and it is the one kind of tab not tied to the workspace root.

Add a mirror entry from the palette with **AgentMux: Mirror an existing tmux session (free mode)…**. Changes take effect after a window reload. Max 12 entries.

id.description: Unique agent id: lower-case, starts with a letter, up to 24 characters. Must not be a built-in id (claude, codex, opencode, hermes, pi, antigravity, devin).

label.description: Tab label. Defaults to the id.

command.description: Command AgentMux runs in a tmux session it creates and manages. Omit when using "session".

args.description: Arguments appended to "command" on every start and resume.

session.description: Free mode: the exact name of an EXISTING tmux session to mirror. AgentMux never creates, restarts or cleans it up. Cannot contain spaces, ':' or '.' (tmux target syntax).

sessionPrefix.description: tmux session prefix for a launch-mode agent. Session = <prefix><folder name>. Defaults to tmux_<id>_.

pane.description: Case-insensitive regular expression matched against the pane's running command, so an instance you started outside AgentMux is adopted. Defaults to the command name.

installCmd.description: Install hint shown by the preflight banner when the command is not on PATH.

accent.description: Tab colour, as #rrggbb. Defaults to a hue derived from the id, so the same id always looks the same.

mark.description: One or two glyphs shown instead of the label once the tab is too narrow for one. Defaults to the first two letters of the label.

modEnter.description: Bytes this agent reads as "newline, do not submit" for Shift+Enter, written as an escape sequence: "\x1b[13;2u" (CSI-u, what Claude, Codex and OpenCode use) or "\x1b[27;2;13~" (xterm modifyOtherKeys, what Hermes, pi and Antigravity use). Leave it out and Shift+Enter submits, as it always has — a wrong sequence types visible garbage into the input box, so it is never guessed.

detection.description: Screen detection rules for this agent, same shape as claudeTmux.detectionRules.

resume.description: Optional resume commands. Templates: {args} expands to "args", {id} to the shell-quoted conversation id.

byId.description: Command that resumes one conversation id, e.g. "aider --session {id} {args}".

claudeTmux.worktrees.description: Start each agent in its own isolated Git worktree (.agentmux/worktrees/<agent>) on branch agent/<agent> to prevent multi-agent file write collisions.

claudeTmux.notifyDone.description: Show a notification when an agent finishes work in the background while its tab is not active or the sidebar is hidden.
